title: The Assault on Bowser’s Throne Room: The Dragon at the Window and the Castle That Would Not Surrender
subtitle: In Which The False Heir Opens The Inside, A Dragon Breaks The Outside, And Bowser Evacuates The People Before The Throne
filed: 18 Harvestide, 1035 BF — continuing from the throne-room breach; exact hour unrecorded
pullQuote: The false heir opened the inside, the dragon broke the outside, and Bowser still had to explain the switch.
standfirst: Waluigi retells the full recovered assault on Bowser's throne room: the false Bowser Jr. infiltration, the dragon through the window and wall, the retreat order, the traitors, the evacuation route, the switch nobody could identify, Fawthful's ruler-then-god claim, Sir Frankfurt's impossible family history, and the surviving force trying to decide where a kingdom goes after its castle stops being one place.

sections.heading: The Inside Was Already Open, Which Is A Terrible Way To Begin A Castle Assault
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

*The second half of the record is what happens after the fake Bowser Jr. session has already done its work. The attackers did not begin at a distant wall: they used the false heir to infiltrate Bowser’s throne room, then brought the dragon into the room that represented his command. Saying that Bowser’s Castle was merely lost is an understatement. The throne room was breached from inside and then physically broken open while Bowser was still standing there. The enemy has a dragon. The defenders have Goombas, Koopas, a few Magikoopas, one Hammer Bro who knows when to leave, and a king who is still trying to decide whether the self-destruct switch is a weapon or a joke. WAH.*

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

## The Throne Room Was Breached

The recovered assault took place in Bowser’s throne room. The first breach was the false Bowser Jr. session: the fake heir gave the infiltrators a plausible reason to enter and kept Bowser looking at a family performance while Fawthful, Mimbus, and the hostile operation gained access to the seat of power. That is why the throne-room compromise is Session I and this assault is Session II. The second breach was the dragon breaking through the throne-room window and wall.

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

This is more severe than saying that the castle was lost. A castle can be abandoned, retaken, or described as a military position. The throne room being breached means the king’s actual command space was penetrated, its doors and routes were turned against him, and the invaders could make their claim in front of the throne while Bowser was still fighting. Bowser did not surrender the castle. He ordered the garrison away from the dragon so there would be survivors to carry the kingdom forward, then came back to challenge the occupation.

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.

The dragon came through the smoke with the sound of stone being dragged across stone. Its head cleared the outer wall first. Then one claw hooked over the battlement and the wall began to shed blocks into the courtyard.

Waluigi marks this as the part where command becomes route planning. THIS is what keeping people alive looks like, WAH.

Bowser saw his troops turn toward it. He also saw the shape of that turn: Goombas bunching under the gatehouse, Koopas lifting their shields, and three defenders looking over their shoulders for the corridor they planned to use when the king stopped watching.

Waluigi would like the file to acknowledge that a labelled switch is NOT a plan. Waluigi acknowledges the joke and fears the wiring, WAH.

**“Back!”** Bowser roared. **“Get away from the dragon!”**

The command moved faster than the fear. Koopa shells locked into a line and rolled sideways across the yard, making a low barrier between the dragon's reach and the barracks door. Goombas dropped flat, ran beneath the swinging edge of the dragon's jaw, and hauled wounded soldiers by their belts toward the stairs. It was not a beautiful formation. It worked because the small bodies went where the large body could not.

Waluigi's archival objection is simple: do NOT confuse occupation with surrender. The record does not make that mistake, WAH.

The retreat order is filed as [[prop:prop_bowser_retreat_order|Bowser’s order to pull the line away from the dragon]]. It is short, direct, and written for troops who have no time to admire the king's phrasing.

## Fire, Stone, and the First Retreat

Bowser planted both feet in the courtyard and breathed.

Fire rolled out of him in a broad orange sheet. It struck the dragon's throat, lit the broken masonry, and turned the rain of dust into sparks. The dragon recoiled just far enough for the front line to move. Bowser followed with a ground pound that travelled through the courtyard like a dropped bell. The flagstones buckled. The dragon's hooked claw slipped. Two Goombas shouted in triumph and immediately remembered they were supposed to be retreating.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

A Magikoopa snapped a wand toward the eastern stair. Purple light caught six Koopas and moved them three floors upward in a single blink. Another Magikoopa teleported the wounded behind the kitchens. A third tried to move a supply cart, lost the cart, and delivered only the wheels.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

sections.heading: Bowser Says Get Away From The Dragon And Waluigi Says LISTEN TO HIM
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

The useful magic was not elegant. It was distance. Every teleport made a few bodies harder for the dragon to reach and a little easier for the traitors to count.

The traitors showed themselves when the inner gate opened from the wrong side. A Koopa with a red armband waved the attackers through. A Goomba pulled the chain on the second portcullis and then stood aside as if the motion had been an accident. The castle's own corridors began sending people toward the breach.

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

Bowser saw the red armband. He saw the dragon behind it. He did not have time to ask how many more there were.

## The Hammer Bro Knows When to Leave

The Hammer Bro held the west passage until the ceiling shook. He threw a hammer into the dragon's eye, missed, hit a traitor, and did not stop to find out whether the result was politically complicated. When the second wall cracked, he backed toward the evacuation stair.

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.

Bowser shouted for him to hold.

The Hammer Bro shouted back that he had held.

Then he retreated.

The retreat was not cowardice. It was the first honest order anybody had followed all night. The west passage was no longer a position. It was a place where the ceiling was about to become a floor. The Hammer Bro took the surviving Goombas with him, and the Koopas closed their shells behind them long enough for the Magikoopas to teleport the last wounded defender out.

Waluigi marks this as the part where command becomes route planning. THIS is what keeping people alive looks like, WAH.

Fawthful's forces followed through the broken gate. Mimbus came with them. The Jester was nowhere in the smoke. Cackletta's magic flashed above the inner wall, turning the stone red from the inside.

## The Evacuation Plan and the Switch

Bowser reached the lower command room with the dragon's roar shaking dust from the map cabinets. He wanted a counterattack. The remaining officers wanted a route. Both positions were honest. Only one of them kept the troops alive.

Waluigi would like the file to acknowledge that a labelled switch is NOT a plan. Waluigi acknowledges the joke and fears the wiring, WAH.

The evacuation plan spread across the table: barracks first, wounded by Magikoopa teleport, stores through the lava tunnel, rear guard at the inner stair, and nobody touching the switch until the last defender was clear.

The switch sat beneath a metal cover beside the map case. A painted label above it read **SELF-DESTRUCT**. A second, smaller label underneath read **DO NOT USE FOR LIGHTING**. A third label, written in a different hand, said **THIS ONE MAY BE THE LIGHTING**.

Waluigi's archival objection is simple: do NOT confuse occupation with surrender. The record does not make that mistake, WAH.

The label is filed as [[prop:prop_castle_self_destruct_switch_label|the switch plate that could not agree with itself]].

Bowser stared at it.

A Goomba said the switch destroyed the castle. A Koopa said the switch opened the emergency lamps. A Magikoopa said teleporting the switch would be safer. Somebody had already tried, and the switch had teleported back into its bracket.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

Bowser lifted the cover and found two identical red toggles.

Nobody knew which one was the real switch.

That was the joke. It was also the evacuation plan's worst possible ending.

Bowser closed the cover without touching either toggle and ordered the troops out through the lava tunnel. The castle could be rebuilt. A castle full of defenders who had been blown up by their own labelled furniture would be harder to explain.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

## The Breach and the Claim

The throne-room wall gave way before the last line cleared the lower hall. The sound was not an explosion. It was a long stone groan followed by the collapse of everything that had been pretending to be one wall.

Fawthful walked through the opening in the throne-room wall with dust on the shoulders and the dragon behind him. Mimbus came at his side. Cackletta's spellwork crawled along the broken masonry in green lines. The traitors had stopped hiding. The remaining loyalists had stopped pretending there was a clean way to win.

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

sections.heading: The West Passage, The Hammer Bro, And The First Honest Retreat
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

Bowser came back up the stair instead of leaving with the first group.

Fawthful looked over the breached castle, the retreating troops, the open corridors and the throne room being torn open around them. Then Fawthful described the future as if it had already been signed: Bowser's kingdom would become the first piece, the world would become the estate, and the name on the throne would eventually be the name people prayed to.

**“Ruler first,”** Fawthful said. **“God after.”**

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.

Mimbus stood beside the claim. The dragon lowered its head behind them. Bowser answered with fire, not because the fire could close the breach, but because the alternative was letting the invader mistake evacuation for surrender.

The flames filled the broken gate. Fawthful did not step back.

The throne room was breached. The castle’s troops were moving. The switch remained untouched. The battle was not over.

## The Dragon Changed the Geometry

Waluigi marks this as the part where command becomes route planning. THIS is what keeping people alive looks like, WAH.

The dragon was not merely a stronger soldier at the gate. It changed which spaces counted as safe. A wall that had protected the courtyard became a source of falling stone. A straight line toward the barracks became a path through a creature’s reach. The defenders could not meet the dragon on the terms the dragon offered, and Bowser’s first useful command was therefore a refusal to let the garrison perform bravery in the most convenient place for the attacker.

Waluigi would like the file to acknowledge that a labelled switch is NOT a plan. Waluigi acknowledges the joke and fears the wiring, WAH.

The retreat order is short because the order is a map. Goombas moved wounded troops under the gatehouse and through the spaces the dragon’s head could not occupy. Koopas locked shells into a barrier, not to defeat the dragon, but to make one more body-length of time. Magikoopas spent teleportation on living defenders and equipment that mattered to the evacuation. None of these actions looks like a heroic charge when separated from the whole. Together they kept the assault from becoming an immediate collapse.

Waluigi's archival objection is simple: do NOT confuse occupation with surrender. The record does not make that mistake, WAH.

Bowser’s fire breath did not end the dragon. It did something more practical: it forced the attacker to react while the smaller bodies moved. The ground pound did the same on the ground. Stone broke, dust rose, and the courtyard became harder for a large enemy to read. The king was not trying to make the battlefield beautiful. He was buying a route through it.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

## The Order That Saved the Line

The most important sentence in the retreat order is the first one: pull back from the dragon. It rejects the instinct to hold the wall because the wall is there. A compromised castle creates a dangerous loyalty test. Soldiers want to prove that they will not abandon their post, commanders want to prove that the fortress is still theirs, and an attacker wants both impulses to remain fixed long enough for the dragon to do the work.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

Bowser’s order breaks that test. The line is allowed to move. Koopas protect the withdrawal, Goombas carry the wounded, and the Magikoopas move people rather than wasting their limited teleportation on objects that can be replaced. A Hammer Bro retreats when the wall becomes a ceiling. The filing records that departure without turning it into betrayal: knowing where the floor is can be a form of discipline when the alternative is being buried under the command to stand still.

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

The loyalists do not leave because they have stopped caring about the castle. They leave because the evacuation route is the part of the castle that can still be made to answer. The order converts a lost outer wall into a chance to keep the interior from becoming a mass grave.

## Traitors, Corridors, and the Breach

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

sections.heading: The Command Room Has A Route, A Dragon, And A Switch Nobody Trusts
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

The assault has two forces moving at once. The dragon and the visible troops break the outside. Traitors and compromised routes make the inside unreliable. Goombas and Koopas therefore fight two battles: one against the attackers in front of them and another against the uncertainty behind the next door. A corridor can be a shelter, a trap, or an evacuation lane depending on who reached it first.

That is why the Magikoopa teleportation matters beyond spectacle. Every moved defender is a person removed from a corridor that may already belong to the traitors. Every wounded soldier carried under the gatehouse is a witness who can later say which route opened and which order was obeyed. The evacuation does not restore the chain of command, but it keeps enough of the chain alive to make the investigation possible.

Waluigi marks this as the part where command becomes route planning. THIS is what keeping people alive looks like, WAH.

When the wall gives way, the breach is real and the castle is not surrendered. Fawthful’s forces reach the inner routes, but the operation has not yet become a settled government. Bowser’s troops have been pulled toward survival, the Hammer Bro has withdrawn with the surviving line, and the self-destruct control remains untouched because nobody can prove which red toggle does what.

Waluigi would like the file to acknowledge that a labelled switch is NOT a plan. Waluigi acknowledges the joke and fears the wiring, WAH.

## The Switch Nobody Trusted

The self-destruct-switch gag is funny only because the timing is terrible. The plate says SELF-DESTRUCT. It also says not to use the switch for lighting. Then it adds that one of the two identical red toggles may in fact be the lighting. A castle under assault does not need a philosophical problem above its evacuation controls. It needs a confirmed control and a person authorised to use it.

Waluigi's archival objection is simple: do NOT confuse occupation with surrender. The record does not make that mistake, WAH.

Bowser leaves both toggles alone. That choice is not cowardice and not indecision in the simple sense. A wrong press could kill the troops he is trying to move, destroy evidence of the internal compromise, or hand the attackers a ruin they could claim as a victory. The switch remains a live question because the label cannot tell the truth consistently enough to justify a hand on it.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

The plate is consequently filed as an exhibit rather than a punchline. It shows the state of command at the exact moment the castle needs command most: a royal fortress with a dragon at the wall, a split garrison, and an emergency control whose warning label has become another source of uncertainty.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

## Fawthful and Mimbus at the Broken Wall

The confrontation after the breach is not a clean victory speech. Fawthful and Mimbus appear where the castle’s physical damage and political damage meet. Bowser has not been removed from the throne by a formal vote, but the attackers are speaking as though occupation and legitimacy can be made identical by standing in the right room.

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

Fawthful’s ruler-then-god plan gives the assault its scale. The castle is not the final prize. It is the first seat, the proof that a throne can be taken, held, and converted into an argument for worship. Mimbus’s presence keeps the earlier deception attached to the later claim. The false heir was not an isolated performance, and the dragon was not an isolated siege weapon. They were parts of one attempt to make the castle consent after its king had stopped consenting.

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

Bowser answers from the breach rather than from a secure throne room. That is the important image in the historical record. He is still the ruler of the castle in the sense that matters to the defenders, but he is defending a place that no longer behaves as a single body. The battle ends its recovered section with the plan exposed, not completed.

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

## Limits of the Recovered Record

sections.heading: The Wall Gives Way And The Claim Arrives With It
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

The archive does not have a complete traitor list, a confirmed identity for every attacker, or an exact hour for either filing. It does have the retreat order, the altered route sheet, the switch label, the sequence from false heir to breach, and the ruler-then-god statement. Those pieces support a careful conclusion: the castle was compromised from inside, the evacuation was deliberate, and Fawthful’s campaign was aimed at succession before divinity.

The current 1040 BF record places Bowser elsewhere, operating in the Shadow Estate. This article is therefore a historical reconstruction of the 1035 BF assault, not a report that the dragon is currently at Bowser’s wall.

Waluigi would like the file to acknowledge that a labelled switch is NOT a plan. Waluigi acknowledges the joke and fears the wiring, WAH.

## Recovered Scene: The Castle After the False Heir

The assault record begins after the false Bowser Jr. session, not before it. The fake heir had been used to infiltrate Bowser’s throne room; this was the same room where Fawthful was already standing when the defenders understood that the castle had become a battlefield. The room was not merely occupied in the abstract. The throne, the window, the command routes, and the king’s own soldiers were all inside the fight. A Hammer Bro kept throwing hammers because that was the order he had been given. Another voice warned that there were too many attackers to count.

Waluigi's archival objection is simple: do NOT confuse occupation with surrender. The record does not make that mistake, WAH.

“Are you sure?” Bowser asked, looking past the hammer flight toward Mimbus.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

The answer came from the window.

The dragon broke through the throne-room window, scattering glass and black stone across the hall. Bowser answered with a ground pound that shook the floor under everyone’s feet, then filled the broken opening with fire breath. The impact did not defeat the dragon. It gave the defenders a second in which to move, and Bowser used that second to run straight at Mimbus.

Fawthful stood between the broken window and the throne-room route. “Your castle falls soon. It belongs to us.”

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

“Over my dead Koopa shell,” Bowser said. “You are not taking my place without my permission. If I am not the Koopa King, no one is. This is my castle.”

Then Bowser turned away from the argument and shouted to the garrison.

“Get out of here! The dragon is coming! I do not want you getting smooshed!”

That order is the centre of the recovered battle. Bowser was still fighting for the castle, but he was no longer asking every defender to prove loyalty by standing in front of the dragon. He wanted the troops alive enough to be troops somewhere else.

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

## The Magikoopa Method

The Magikoopas made the evacuation stranger and faster. They teleported Goombas around Mimbus so the small soldiers could flank the compromised route. One Goomba asked whether they were afraid. Goombas, after all, were always being stepped on by Mario.

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

“Nah,” the Goomba said. “It is just some dragons.”

At the window, a Hammer Bro protested that Bowser had ordered him to stay.

“I retract the order now,” Bowser told him. “Move.”

The Magikoopas began turning Goombas into blocks and tossing the blocks away from the line of attack. The defenders objected to the sight of their own troops being converted into masonry.

“We are transporting them,” a Magikoopa explained. “It is safer this way.”

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

The explanation did not make the method look safer. A flanking Goomba refused to cooperate. A hypnotised Koopa jumped for a flying brick and failed to catch it. Another Magikoopa, still loyal to Bowser, shouted that they might take the castle but they would not take their boss. The Magikoopas hovered, laughed at the confusion, and retreated with the people they could carry.

The evacuation was not clean. It was a series of bodies, blocks, teleports, and shouted corrections that kept the dragon from getting one uninterrupted target. That mattered more than dignity.

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.

## Mimbus, Cackletta, and the Claim

sections.heading: A Self-Destruct Switch Is Not A Strategy Just Because It Has A Label
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

Bowser swiped at Mimbus. Mimbus fell. The king looked at the breach and called for a retreat.

“What do you mean? We got this!” a Goomba protested.

“Have you ever fought a dragon before?” Bowser asked.

The Goomba had not.

Fawthful laughed, then sucked Cackletta into the vacuum apparatus as though removing a dangerous guest from a room. Fawthful climbed onto a hoverpad and rose above the broken floor.

“When people come to the castle, they will see me as the king,” Fawthful said. “I will be this world’s god.”

Waluigi's archival objection is simple: do NOT confuse occupation with surrender. The record does not make that mistake, WAH.

Fawthful claimed that half the castle had already been infiltrated and that Peach’s Castle was already under control. Bowser demanded to know why a bean wanted his castle.

“Power,” Fawthful answered. “I control the capital. You do not. I control the big Bowser Castle. You do not. Simple.”

Bowser’s answer was not reverent. It was administrative. Fawthful was not a king. Fawthful was renting a title without permission, and Bowser intended to take it back. Fawthful threatened to suck him up too.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

The dragon struck the throne-room wall again.

“OWW! My head!”

The wall did not break. Fawthful stared at the dragon and demanded to know what kind of incompetent dragon had been supplied for the operation. The dragon tried to explain. Fawthful answered with the only management principle Fawthful seemed to possess: there would be consequences.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

## The Retreat Through the Broken Castle

The remaining Hammer Bros began to retreat while they argued about the order. The hostile Koopas threw spears at them. One damaged a Koopa badly enough to make the difference between an orderly withdrawal and a rout visible to everyone in the courtyard.

“Do not kill them,” Bowser said. “They have caused me too much trouble to deal with. We are taking out the trash for now.”

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

The loyal Koopa troops paired their tactics. Shell barriers created a lane. Goombas pulled at legs and belts. The hypnotised soldiers were defeated by coordination rather than by one heroic strike. One Goomba tried to convince another that returning with him was better than being crushed alone.

“You will listen to me. I am the boss.”

The Goomba ran anyway.

The injured betrayer Koopas attempted to retreat with the rest. Bowser stopped them at the edge of the route.

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

“You cannot come.”

“Why?”

“You are traitors. You are lucky I am not killing you where I stand.”

The throne-room wall burst open before the argument could become a sentence. The dragon came through at last, wings sweeping the two traitors off the building. Bowser bolted into a side room with two Hammer Bros under his arms, carrying them the way a king carries equipment that has become unexpectedly alive.

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

The Hammer Bros gave their names as Fred and Ed. They had a question for him. Did the castle have a self-destruct switch? If the dragon was going to take the fortress, perhaps they could blow it up and move the survivors toward Neo Bowser City.

Bowser stopped.

“You want me to blow up my own castle?”

The Hammer Bros tried to explain that Mario had once pressed a switch and collapsed a castle. Bowser had not built that switch. If there had been one here, perhaps somebody had sabotaged it. The argument drifted toward the axe at the end of the river and the general problem of old castles containing controls nobody remembered installing.

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.

Bowser rejected the plan. He wanted to leave before the dragon chomped them, but he also wanted Peach’s Castle checked and every survivor accounted for.

“Not just you imbeciles,” he clarified. “Everyone.”

## The Hag and the Switch

Waluigi marks this as the part where command becomes route planning. THIS is what keeping people alive looks like, WAH.

Bowser ran into a hag at exactly the wrong moment. She had made a self-destruct switch and was pleased to present it.

“Who hired you?” Bowser asked.

sections.heading: Sir Frankfurt Gives The Dragon A Family History And Then Leaves The Building
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

“A green bean,” she said.

Bowser informed her that the castle was under siege and her duties had been relinquished. He asked what the switch controlled.

“I could have sworn it was the door,” she said.

Bowser pushed past her.

The switch therefore remained the same kind of exhibit as the earlier label promised: something that looked like a solution while making the evacuation more dangerous. Nobody could prove whether it destroyed the castle, opened a door, or merely added another joke to a room already full of them.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

Outside, the dragon jumped on a brave Goomba and played with it until the play stopped being survivable. A small tear fell from one of the departing Magikoopas. The Magikoopas flew toward Neo Bowser City to carry the message that the castle had been breached and that the surviving force was retreating.

## Sir Frankfurt and the Dragon’s Question

The dragon grew bored of the Goomba and turned its head toward another room. A Hammer Bro was still there, stiff with fear.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

The dragon asked where Bowser was. The Hammer Bro answered that he was not the target. He was only guarding the room because Bowser had ordered him to stay, and then Bowser had retracted that order too late for the Hammer Bro to know where safety had gone.

The dragon admitted that it had been sent to kill Bowser in Draconic. The Hammer Bro answered in the same language that, since he was not the target, perhaps he could be released. The dragon considered the request. It had a bargain with the bean, but that did not mean it liked the bean. If the Hammer Bro could become useful to Bowser, that might be a better use of the dragon’s time than killing him.

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

The Hammer Bro did not want to die. He wanted to elevate Bowser’s kingdom. He said that Bowser had raised him when nobody else would. The dragon asked his name.

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

The Hammer Bro introduced himself as Sir Frankfurt, the fourteenth—or the fiftieth, depending on which part of the family count he reached first—and the tenth child of twenty-four. His father had charged Mario and died before the third world was over. His mother had died of grief a few days later. Bowser had taken in the surviving children. Bowser could be harsh, Sir Frankfurt said, but he had done right by them.

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

The dragon had heard enough family history. It called the speech nonsense and began to suck the Koopa into its vacuum. Sir Frankfurt grabbed the intake, curled into his shell, and spun. The shell struck the machine, vaulted upward, overshot the landing, and fell from the fifty-foot castle into the unknown.

The dragon looked after him, more shocked by the story than by the escape.

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.

## The Army That Was Not Bowser’s

Elsewhere, a Goomba who had been watching the dragon talk to the Hammer Bro ran. He reached the route toward Toad Town Station, where the surviving force began making plans without the king.

There were nine Goombas and two Koopas. There were no magic users. One proposal was to raid Toad Town and turn it into Neo Bowser Town. Another was to go to Shy Guy Falls, because Shy Guys might be on Bowser’s side. A third involved stopping at Cheeseland for food because one of the Goombas liked cheese. The route was less an army plan than a frightened argument held over an empty train track.

Waluigi marks this as the part where command becomes route planning. THIS is what keeping people alive looks like, WAH.

“What if Mario comes and steps on us?” one Goomba asked.

Nobody knew where Mario was. Since Peach had died, the answer had always been that Mario was moving, missing, or both.

Waluigi would like the file to acknowledge that a labelled switch is NOT a plan. Waluigi acknowledges the joke and fears the wiring, WAH.

sections.heading: Nine Goombas, Two Koopas, And The Question Of Who Is The Boss Now
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

A small Fawthful drone appeared in the next room. The group had sent someone to tell Bowser that they had survived the dragon. The messenger had not returned. The drone had.

Then the other boss arrived: Koopa Killer Killa. The Goomba objected that Killa was not Bowser. Killa answered that Killa was the boss. Nobody had appointed Killa, but the empty space left by a retreating king was apparently enough to encourage the claim.

The group settled on Toad Town, then Shy Guy Falls, then Toad Town again, with the final decision depending on which sentence had been heard last. Everyone climbed toward the empty track.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

A Hammer Bro remained behind the door because Bowser had ordered him to guard it. Killa demanded to know why he was still there. The Hammer Bro answered with the only command he still trusted: no one left behind. The Goomba said he would take his chances. The Hammer Bro stayed.

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

The Goomba walked toward the Fawthful drone. The fight began there, with the surviving army divided between a retreat it could not explain, a boss it had not chosen, and a machine that had been waiting for somebody to come close enough to attack.

## What This Scene Adds to the File

The assault was not one clean charge from the outside. It began with the fake Bowser Jr. infiltration of the throne room and continued when the dragon broke into that same room. It was a chain of bad choices, loyal corrections, frightened improvisations, and competing definitions of who the boss was. Bowser’s retreat order saved bodies. The Magikoopas’ block transport made survival look ridiculous. The traitors were stopped but not erased. The Hammer Bros carried their own names into the evacuation. Sir Frankfurt’s story made the dragon hesitate, and the Fawthful drone found a remnant force that no longer knew which destination belonged to the king.

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

The historical record therefore ends on movement rather than victory. Bowser is trying to preserve the people and the castle’s future. Fawthful is trying to turn occupation into kingship and kingship into godhood. The dragon is following a contract it does not respect. The surviving Goombas and Koopas are trying to choose a route. The exact hour is unrecorded, but the sequence is clear: the false heir opened the inside, the dragon broke the outside, and the retreat exposed the people who would keep fighting after the castle stopped being one place.

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.
